paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 30 段）

paragraphs.en: `If everybody minded their own business,' the Duchess said in a hoarse growl, `the world would go round a deal faster than it does.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 31 段）

paragraphs.en: `Which would NOT be an advantage,' said Alice, who felt very glad to get an opportunity of showing off a little of her knowledge. `Just think of what work it would make with the day and night! You see the earth takes twenty-four hours to turn round on its axis--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 32 段）

paragraphs.en: `Talking of axes,' said the Duchess, `chop off her head!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 33 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice glanced rather anxiously at the cook, to see if she meant to take the hint; but the cook was busily stirring the soup, and seemed not to be listening, so she went on again: `Twenty-four hours, I THINK; or is it twelve? I--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 34 段）

paragraphs.en: `Oh, don't bother ME,' said the Duchess; `I never could abide figures!' And with that she began nursing her child again, singing a sort of lullaby to it as she did so, and giving it a violent shake at the end of every line:
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 35 段）

paragraphs.en: `Speak roughly to your little boy, And beat him when he sneezes: He only does it to annoy, Because he knows it teases.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 36 段）

paragraphs.en: CHORUS.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 37 段）

paragraphs.en: (In which the cook and the baby joined):--
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 38 段）

paragraphs.en: `Wow! wow! wow!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 39 段）

paragraphs.en: While the Duchess sang the second verse of the song, she kept tossing the baby violently up and down, and the poor little thing howled so, that Alice could hardly hear the words:--
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 40 段）

paragraphs.en: `I speak severely to my boy, I beat him when he sneezes; For he can thoroughly enjoy The pepper when he pleases!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 41 段）

paragraphs.en: CHORUS.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 42 段）

paragraphs.en: `Wow! wow! wow!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 43 段）

paragraphs.en: `Here! you may nurse it a bit, if you like!' the Duchess said to Alice, flinging the baby at her as she spoke. `I must go and get ready to play croquet with the Queen,' and she hurried out of the room. The cook threw a frying-pan after her as she went out, but it just missed her.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 44 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice caught the baby with some difficulty, as it was a queer- shaped little creature, and held out its arms and legs in all directions, `just like a star-fish,' thought Alice. The poor little thing was snorting like a steam-engine when she caught it, and kept doubling itself up and straightening itself out again, so that altogether, for the first minute or two, it was as much as she could do to hold it.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 45 段）

paragraphs.en: As soon as she had made out the proper way of nursing it, (which was to twist it up into a sort of knot, and then keep tight hold of its right ear and left foot, so as to prevent its undoing itself,) she carried it out into the open air. `IF I don't take this child away with me,' thought Alice, `they're sure to kill it in a day or two: wouldn't it be murder to leave it behind?' She said the last words out loud, and the little thing grunted in reply (it had left off sneezing by this time). `Don't grunt,' said Alice; `that's not at all a proper way of expressing yourself.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 46 段）

paragraphs.en: The baby grunted again, and Alice looked very anxiously into its face to see what was the matter with it. There could be no doubt that it had a VERY turn-up nose, much more like a snout than a real nose; also its eyes were getting extremely small for a baby: altogether Alice did not like the look of the thing at all. `But perhaps it was only sobbing,' she thought, and looked into its eyes again, to see if there were any tears.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 47 段）

paragraphs.en: No, there were no tears. `If you're going to turn into a pig, my dear,' said Alice, seriously, `I'll have nothing more to do with you. Mind now!' The poor little thing sobbed again (or grunted, it was impossible to say which), and they went on for some while in silence.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 48 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice was just beginning to think to herself, `Now, what am I to do with this creature when I get it home?' when it grunted again, so violently, that she looked down into its face in some alarm. This time there could be NO mistake about it: it was neither more nor less than a pig, and she felt that it would be quite absurd for her to carry it further.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 49 段）

paragraphs.en: So she set the little creature down, and felt quite relieved to see it trot away quietly into the wood. `If it had grown up,' she said to herself, `it would have made a dreadfully ugly child: but it makes rather a handsome pig, I think.' And she began thinking over other children she knew, who might do very well as pigs, and was just saying to herself, `if one only knew the right way to change them--' when she was a little startled by seeing the Cheshire Cat sitting on a bough of a tree a few yards off.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 50 段）

paragraphs.en: The Cat only grinned when it saw Alice. It looked good- natured, she thought: still it had VERY long claws and a great many teeth, so she felt that it ought to be treated with respect.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 51 段）

paragraphs.en: `Cheshire Puss,' she began, rather timidly, as she did not at all know whether it would like the name: however, it only grinned a little wider. `Come, it's pleased so far,' thought Alice, and she went on. `Would you tell me, please, which way I ought to go from here?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 52 段）

paragraphs.en: `That depends a good deal on where you want to get to,' said the Cat.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 53 段）

paragraphs.en: `I don't much care where--' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 54 段）

paragraphs.en: `Then it doesn't matter which way you go,' said the Cat.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 55 段）

paragraphs.en: `--so long as I get SOMEWHERE,' Alice added as an explanation.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 56 段）

paragraphs.en: `Oh, you're sure to do that,' said the Cat, `if you only walk long enough.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 57 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice felt that this could not be denied, so she tried another question. `What sort of people live about here?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 58 段）

paragraphs.en: `In THAT direction,' the Cat said, waving its right paw round, `lives a Hatter: and in THAT direction,' waving the other paw, `lives a March Hare. Visit either you like: they're both mad.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 59 段）

paragraphs.en: `But I don't want to go among mad people,' Alice remarked.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 60 段）

paragraphs.en: `Oh, you can't help that,' said the Cat: `we're all mad here. I'm mad. You're mad.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 61 段）

paragraphs.en: `How do you know I'm mad?' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 62 段）

paragraphs.en: `You must be,' said the Cat, `or you wouldn't have come here.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 63 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice didn't think that proved it at all; however, she went on `And how do you know that you're mad?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 64 段）

paragraphs.en: `To begin with,' said the Cat, `a dog's not mad. You grant that?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 65 段）

paragraphs.en: `I suppose so,' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 66 段）

paragraphs.en: `Well, then,' the Cat went on, `you see, a dog growls when it's angry, and wags its tail when it's pleased. Now I growl when I'm pleased, and wag my tail when I'm angry. Therefore I'm mad.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 67 段）

paragraphs.en: `I call it purring, not growling,' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 68 段）

paragraphs.en: `Call it what you like,' said the Cat. `Do you play croquet with the Queen to-day?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 69 段）

paragraphs.en: `I should like it very much,' said Alice, `but I haven't been invited yet.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 70 段）

paragraphs.en: `You'll see me there,' said the Cat, and vanished.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 71 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice was not much surprised at this, she was getting so used to queer things happening. While she was looking at the place where it had been, it suddenly appeared again.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 72 段）

paragraphs.en: `By-the-bye, what became of the baby?' said the Cat. `I'd nearly forgotten to ask.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 73 段）

paragraphs.en: `It turned into a pig,' Alice quietly said, just as if it had come back in a natural way.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 74 段）

paragraphs.en: `I thought it would,' said the Cat, and vanished again.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 75 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice waited a little, half expecting to see it again, but it did not appear, and after a minute or two she walked on in the direction in which the March Hare was said to live. `I've seen hatters before,' she said to herself; `the March Hare will be much the most interesting, and perhaps as this is May it won't be raving mad--at least not so mad as it was in March.' As she said this, she looked up, and there was the Cat again, sitting on a branch of a tree.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 76 段）

paragraphs.en: `Did you say pig, or fig?' said the Cat.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 77 段）

paragraphs.en: `I said pig,' replied Alice; `and I wish you wouldn't keep appearing and vanishing so suddenly: you make one quite giddy.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 78 段）

paragraphs.en: `All right,' said the Cat; and this time it vanished quite slowly, beginning with the end of the tail, and ending with the grin, which remained some time after the rest of it had gone.
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 79 段）

paragraphs.en: `Well! I've often seen a cat without a grin,' thought Alice; `but a grin without a cat! It's the most curious thing I ever saw in my life!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 80 段）

paragraphs.en: She had not gone much farther before she came in sight of the house of the March Hare: she thought it must be the right house, because the chimneys were shaped like ears and the roof was thatched with fur. It was so large a house, that she did not like to go nearer till she had nibbled some more of the lefthand bit of mushroom, and raised herself to about two feet high: even then she walked up towards it rather timidly, saying to herself `Suppose it should be raving mad after all! I almost wish I'd gone to see the Hatter instead!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 6 章 · 小猪与胡椒 第 81 段）

paragraphs.en:
CHAPTER VII
A Mad Tea-Party
paragraphs.zh: 第七章 · 疯狂下午茶
paragraphs.chapterTitleZh: 第七章 · 疯狂下午茶

paragraphs.en: There was a table set out under a tree in front of the house, and the March Hare and the Hatter were having tea at it: a Dormouse was sitting between them, fast asleep, and the other two were using it as a cushion, resting their elbows on it, and talking over its head. `Very uncomfortable for the Dormouse,' thought Alice; `only, as it's asleep, I suppose it doesn't mind.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 1 段）

paragraphs.en: The table was a large one, but the three were all crowded together at one corner of it: `No room! No room!' they cried out when they saw Alice coming. `There's PLENTY of room!' said Alice indignantly, and she sat down in a large arm-chair at one end of the table.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 2 段）

paragraphs.en: `Have some wine,' the March Hare said in an encouraging tone.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 3 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice looked all round the table, but there was nothing on it but tea. `I don't see any wine,' she remarked.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 4 段）

paragraphs.en: `There isn't any,' said the March Hare.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 5 段）

paragraphs.en: `Then it wasn't very civil of you to offer it,' said Alice angrily.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 6 段）

paragraphs.en: `It wasn't very civil of you to sit down without being invited,' said the March Hare.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 7 段）

paragraphs.en: `I didn't know it was YOUR table,' said Alice; `it's laid for a great many more than three.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 8 段）

paragraphs.en: `Your hair wants cutting,' said the Hatter. He had been looking at Alice for some time with great curiosity, and this was his first speech.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 9 段）

paragraphs.en: `You should learn not to make personal remarks,' Alice said with some severity; `it's very rude.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 10 段）

paragraphs.en: The Hatter opened his eyes very wide on hearing this; but all he SAID was, `Why is a raven like a writing-desk?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 11 段）

paragraphs.en: `Come, we shall have some fun now!' thought Alice. `I'm glad they've begun asking riddles.--I believe I can guess that,' she added aloud.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 12 段）

paragraphs.en: `Do you mean that you think you can find out the answer to it?' said the March Hare.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 13 段）

paragraphs.en: `Exactly so,' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 14 段）

paragraphs.en: `Then you should say what you mean,' the March Hare went on.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 15 段）

paragraphs.en: `I do,' Alice hastily replied; `at least--at least I mean what I say--that's the same thing, you know.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 16 段）

paragraphs.en: `Not the same thing a bit!' said the Hatter. `You might just as well say that "I see what I eat" is the same thing as "I eat what I see"!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 17 段）

paragraphs.en: `You might just as well say,' added the March Hare, `that "I like what I get" is the same thing as "I get what I like"!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 18 段）

paragraphs.en: `You might just as well say,' added the Dormouse, who seemed to be talking in his sleep, `that "I breathe when I sleep" is the same thing as "I sleep when I breathe"!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 19 段）

paragraphs.en: `It IS the same thing with you,' said the Hatter, and here the conversation dropped, and the party sat silent for a minute, while Alice thought over all she could remember about ravens and writing-desks, which wasn't much.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 20 段）

paragraphs.en: The Hatter was the first to break the silence. `What day of the month is it?' he said, turning to Alice: he had taken his watch out of his pocket, and was looking at it uneasily, shaking it every now and then, and holding it to his ear.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 21 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice considered a little, and then said `The fourth.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 22 段）

paragraphs.en: `Two days wrong!' sighed the Hatter. `I told you butter wouldn't suit the works!' he added looking angrily at the March Hare.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 23 段）

paragraphs.en: `It was the BEST butter,' the March Hare meekly replied.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 24 段）

paragraphs.en: `Yes, but some crumbs must have got in as well,' the Hatter grumbled: `you shouldn't have put it in with the bread-knife.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 25 段）

paragraphs.en: The March Hare took the watch and looked at it gloomily: then he dipped it into his cup of tea, and looked at it again: but he could think of nothing better to say than his first remark, `It was the BEST butter, you know.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 26 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice had been looking over his shoulder with some curiosity. `What a funny watch!' she remarked. `It tells the day of the month, and doesn't tell what o'clock it is!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 27 段）

paragraphs.en: `Why should it?' muttered the Hatter. `Does YOUR watch tell you what year it is?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 28 段）

paragraphs.en: `Of course not,' Alice replied very readily: `but that's because it stays the same year for such a long time together.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 29 段）

paragraphs.en: `Which is just the case with MINE,' said the Hatter.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 30 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice felt dreadfully puzzled. The Hatter's remark seemed to have no sort of meaning in it, and yet it was certainly English. `I don't quite understand you,' she said, as politely as she could.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 31 段）

paragraphs.en: `The Dormouse is asleep again,' said the Hatter, and he poured a little hot tea upon its nose.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 32 段）

paragraphs.en: The Dormouse shook its head impatiently, and said, without opening its eyes, `Of course, of course; just what I was going to remark myself.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 33 段）

paragraphs.en: `Have you guessed the riddle yet?' the Hatter said, turning to Alice again.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 34 段）

paragraphs.en: `No, I give it up,' Alice replied: `what's the answer?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 35 段）

paragraphs.en: `I haven't the slightest idea,' said the Hatter.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 36 段）

paragraphs.en: `Nor I,' said the March Hare.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 37 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice sighed wearily. `I think you might do something better with the time,' she said, `than waste it in asking riddles that have no answers.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 38 段）

paragraphs.en: `If you knew Time as well as I do,' said the Hatter, `you wouldn't talk about wasting IT. It's HIM.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 39 段）

paragraphs.en: `I don't know what you mean,' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 40 段）

paragraphs.en: `Of course you don't!' the Hatter said, tossing his head contemptuously. `I dare say you never even spoke to Time!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 41 段）

paragraphs.en: `Perhaps not,' Alice cautiously replied: `but I know I have to beat time when I learn music.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 42 段）

paragraphs.en: `Ah! that accounts for it,' said the Hatter. `He won't stand beating. Now, if you only kept on good terms with him, he'd do almost anything you liked with the clock. For instance, suppose it were nine o'clock in the morning, just time to begin lessons: you'd only have to whisper a hint to Time, and round goes the clock in a twinkling! Half-past one, time for dinner!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 43 段）

paragraphs.en: (`I only wish it was,' the March Hare said to itself in a whisper.)
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 44 段）

paragraphs.en: `That would be grand, certainly,' said Alice thoughtfully: `but then--I shouldn't be hungry for it, you know.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 45 段）

paragraphs.en: `Not at first, perhaps,' said the Hatter: `but you could keep it to half-past one as long as you liked.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 46 段）

paragraphs.en: `Is that the way YOU manage?' Alice asked.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 47 段）

paragraphs.en: The Hatter shook his head mournfully. `Not I!' he replied. `We quarrelled last March--just before HE went mad, you know--' (pointing with his tea spoon at the March Hare,) `--it was at the great concert given by the Queen of Hearts, and I had to sing
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 48 段）

paragraphs.en: "Twinkle, twinkle, little bat! How I wonder what you're at!"
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 49 段）

paragraphs.en: You know the song, perhaps?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 50 段）

paragraphs.en: `I've heard something like it,' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 51 段）

paragraphs.en: `It goes on, you know,' the Hatter continued, `in this way:--
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 52 段）

paragraphs.en: "Up above the world you fly, Like a tea-tray in the sky. Twinkle, twinkle--"'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 53 段）

paragraphs.en: Here the Dormouse shook itself, and began singing in its sleep `Twinkle, twinkle, twinkle, twinkle--' and went on so long that they had to pinch it to make it stop.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 54 段）

paragraphs.en: `Well, I'd hardly finished the first verse,' said the Hatter, `when the Queen jumped up and bawled out, "He's murdering the time! Off with his head!"'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 55 段）

paragraphs.en: `How dreadfully savage!' exclaimed Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 56 段）

paragraphs.en: `And ever since that,' the Hatter went on in a mournful tone, `he won't do a thing I ask! It's always six o'clock now.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 57 段）

paragraphs.en: A bright idea came into Alice's head. `Is that the reason so many tea-things are put out here?' she asked.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 58 段）

paragraphs.en: `Yes, that's it,' said the Hatter with a sigh: `it's always tea-time, and we've no time to wash the things between whiles.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 59 段）

paragraphs.en: `Then you keep moving round, I suppose?' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 60 段）

paragraphs.en: `Exactly so,' said the Hatter: `as the things get used up.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 61 段）

paragraphs.en: `But what happens when you come to the beginning again?' Alice ventured to ask.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 62 段）

paragraphs.en: `Suppose we change the subject,' the March Hare interrupted, yawning. `I'm getting tired of this. I vote the young lady tells us a story.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 63 段）

paragraphs.en: `I'm afraid I don't know one,' said Alice, rather alarmed at the proposal.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 64 段）

paragraphs.en: `Then the Dormouse shall!' they both cried. `Wake up, Dormouse!' And they pinched it on both sides at once.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 65 段）

paragraphs.en: The Dormouse slowly opened his eyes. `I wasn't asleep,' he said in a hoarse, feeble voice: `I heard every word you fellows were saying.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 66 段）

paragraphs.en: `Tell us a story!' said the March Hare.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 67 段）

paragraphs.en: `Yes, please do!' pleaded Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 68 段）

paragraphs.en: `And be quick about it,' added the Hatter, `or you'll be asleep again before it's done.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 69 段）

paragraphs.en: `Once upon a time there were three little sisters,' the Dormouse began in a great hurry; `and their names were Elsie, Lacie, and Tillie; and they lived at the bottom of a well--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 70 段）

paragraphs.en: `What did they live on?' said Alice, who always took a great interest in questions of eating and drinking.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 71 段）

paragraphs.en: `They lived on treacle,' said the Dormouse, after thinking a minute or two.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 72 段）

paragraphs.en: `They couldn't have done that, you know,' Alice gently remarked; `they'd have been ill.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 73 段）

paragraphs.en: `So they were,' said the Dormouse; `VERY ill.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 74 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice tried to fancy to herself what such an extraordinary ways of living would be like, but it puzzled her too much, so she went on: `But why did they live at the bottom of a well?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 75 段）

paragraphs.en: `Take some more tea,' the March Hare said to Alice, very earnestly.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 76 段）

paragraphs.en: `I've had nothing yet,' Alice replied in an offended tone, `so I can't take more.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 77 段）

paragraphs.en: `You mean you can't take LESS,' said the Hatter: `it's very easy to take MORE than nothing.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 78 段）

paragraphs.en: `Nobody asked YOUR opinion,' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 79 段）

paragraphs.en: `Who's making personal remarks now?' the Hatter asked triumphantly.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 80 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice did not quite know what to say to this: so she helped herself to some tea and bread-and-butter, and then turned to the Dormouse, and repeated her question. `Why did they live at the bottom of a well?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 81 段）

paragraphs.en: The Dormouse again took a minute or two to think about it, and then said, `It was a treacle-well.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 82 段）

paragraphs.en: `There's no such thing!' Alice was beginning very angrily, but the Hatter and the March Hare went `Sh! sh!' and the Dormouse sulkily remarked, `If you can't be civil, you'd better finish the story for yourself.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 83 段）

paragraphs.en: `No, please go on!' Alice said very humbly; `I won't interrupt again. I dare say there may be ONE.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 84 段）

paragraphs.en: `One, indeed!' said the Dormouse indignantly. However, he consented to go on. `And so these three little sisters--they were learning to draw, you know--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 85 段）

paragraphs.en: `What did they draw?' said Alice, quite forgetting her promise.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 86 段）

paragraphs.en: `Treacle,' said the Dormouse, without considering at all this time.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 87 段）

paragraphs.en: `I want a clean cup,' interrupted the Hatter: `let's all move one place on.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 88 段）

paragraphs.en: He moved on as he spoke, and the Dormouse followed him: the March Hare moved into the Dormouse's place, and Alice rather unwillingly took the place of the March Hare. The Hatter was the only one who got any advantage from the change: and Alice was a good deal worse off than before, as the March Hare had just upset the milk-jug into his plate.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 89 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice did not wish to offend the Dormouse again, so she began very cautiously: `But I don't understand. Where did they draw the treacle from?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 90 段）

paragraphs.en: `You can draw water out of a water-well,' said the Hatter; `so I should think you could draw treacle out of a treacle-well--eh, stupid?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 91 段）

paragraphs.en: `But they were IN the well,' Alice said to the Dormouse, not choosing to notice this last remark.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 92 段）

paragraphs.en: `Of course they were', said the Dormouse; `--well in.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 93 段）

paragraphs.en: This answer so confused poor Alice, that she let the Dormouse go on for some time without interrupting it.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 94 段）

paragraphs.en: `They were learning to draw,' the Dormouse went on, yawning and rubbing its eyes, for it was getting very sleepy; `and they drew all manner of things--everything that begins with an M--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 95 段）

paragraphs.en: `Why with an M?' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 96 段）

paragraphs.en: `Why not?' said the March Hare.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 97 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice was silent.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 98 段）

paragraphs.en: The Dormouse had closed its eyes by this time, and was going off into a doze; but, on being pinched by the Hatter, it woke up again with a little shriek, and went on: `--that begins with an M, such as mouse-traps, and the moon, and memory, and muchness-- you know you say things are "much of a muchness"--did you ever see such a thing as a drawing of a muchness?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 99 段）

paragraphs.en: `Really, now you ask me,' said Alice, very much confused, `I don't think--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 100 段）

paragraphs.en: `Then you shouldn't talk,' said the Hatter.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 101 段）

paragraphs.en: This piece of rudeness was more than Alice could bear: she got up in great disgust, and walked off; the Dormouse fell asleep instantly, and neither of the others took the least notice of her going, though she looked back once or twice, half hoping that they would call after her: the last time she saw them, they were trying to put the Dormouse into the teapot.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 102 段）

paragraphs.en: `At any rate I'll never go THERE again!' said Alice as she picked her way through the wood. `It's the stupidest tea-party I ever was at in all my life!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 103 段）

paragraphs.en: Just as she said this, she noticed that one of the trees had a door leading right into it. `That's very curious!' she thought. `But everything's curious today. I think I may as well go in at once.' And in she went.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 104 段）

paragraphs.en: Once more she found herself in the long hall, and close to the little glass table. `Now, I'll manage better this time,' she said to herself, and began by taking the little golden key, and unlocking the door that led into the garden. Then she went to work nibbling at the mushroom (she had kept a piece of it in her pocket) till she was about a foot high: then she walked down the little passage: and THEN--she found herself at last in the beautiful garden, among the bright flower-beds and the cool fountains.
paragraphs.zh: （第 7 章 · 疯狂下午茶 第 105 段）

paragraphs.en:
CHAPTER VIII
The Queen's Croquet-Ground
paragraphs.zh: 第八章 · 王后的槌球场
paragraphs.chapterTitleZh: 第八章 · 王后的槌球场

paragraphs.en: A large rose-tree stood near the entrance of the garden: the roses growing on it were white, but there were three gardeners at it, busily painting them red. Alice thought this a very curious thing, and she went nearer to watch them, and just as she came up to them she heard one of them say, `Look out now, Five! Don't go splashing paint over me like that!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 1 段）

paragraphs.en: `I couldn't help it,' said Five, in a sulky tone; `Seven jogged my elbow.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 2 段）

paragraphs.en: On which Seven looked up and said, `That's right, Five! Always lay the blame on others!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 3 段）

paragraphs.en: `YOU'D better not talk!' said Five. `I heard the Queen say only yesterday you deserved to be beheaded!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 4 段）

paragraphs.en: `What for?' said the one who had spoken first.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 5 段）

paragraphs.en: `That's none of YOUR business, Two!' said Seven.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 6 段）

paragraphs.en: `Yes, it IS his business!' said Five, `and I'll tell him--it was for bringing the cook tulip-roots instead of onions.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 7 段）

paragraphs.en: Seven flung down his brush, and had just begun `Well, of all the unjust things--' when his eye chanced to fall upon Alice, as she stood watching them, and he checked himself suddenly: the others looked round also, and all of them bowed low.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 8 段）

paragraphs.en: `Would you tell me,' said Alice, a little timidly, `why you are painting those roses?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 9 段）

paragraphs.en: Five and Seven said nothing, but looked at Two. Two began in a low voice, `Why the fact is, you see, Miss, this here ought to have been a RED rose-tree, and we put a white one in by mistake; and if the Queen was to find it out, we should all have our heads cut off, you know. So you see, Miss, we're doing our best, afore she comes, to--' At this moment Five, who had been anxiously looking across the garden, called out `The Queen! The Queen!' and the three gardeners instantly threw themselves flat upon their faces. There was a sound of many footsteps, and Alice looked round, eager to see the Queen.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 10 段）

paragraphs.en: First came ten soldiers carrying clubs; these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners: next the ten courtiers; these were ornamented all over with diamonds, and walked two and two, as the soldiers did. After these came the royal children; there were ten of them, and the little dears came jumping merrily along hand in hand, in couples: they were all ornamented with hearts. Next came the guests, mostly Kings and Queens, and among them Alice recognised the White Rabbit: it was talking in a hurried nervous manner, smiling at everything that was said, and went by without noticing her. Then followed the Knave of Hearts, carrying the King's crown on a crimson velvet cushion; and, last of all this grand procession, came THE KING AND QUEEN OF HEARTS.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 11 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice was rather doubtful whether she ought not to lie down on her face like the three gardeners, but she could not remember ever having heard of such a rule at processions; `and besides, what would be the use of a procession,' thought she, `if people had all to lie down upon their faces, so that they couldn't see it?' So she stood still where she was, and waited.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 12 段）

paragraphs.en: When the procession came opposite to Alice, they all stopped and looked at her, and the Queen said severely `Who is this?' She said it to the Knave of Hearts, who only bowed and smiled in reply.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 13 段）

paragraphs.en: `Idiot!' said the Queen, tossing her head impatiently; and, turning to Alice, she went on, `What's your name, child?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 14 段）

paragraphs.en: `My name is Alice, so please your Majesty,' said Alice very politely; but she added, to herself, `Why, they're only a pack of cards, after all. I needn't be afraid of them!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 15 段）

paragraphs.en: `And who are THESE?' said the Queen, pointing to the three gardeners who were lying round the rosetree; for, you see, as they were lying on their faces, and the pattern on their backs was the same as the rest of the pack, she could not tell whether they were gardeners, or soldiers, or courtiers, or three of her own children.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 16 段）

paragraphs.en: `How should I know?' said Alice, surprised at her own courage. `It's no business of MINE.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 17 段）

paragraphs.en: The Queen turned crimson with fury, and, after glaring at her for a moment like a wild beast, screamed `Off with her head! Off--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 18 段）

paragraphs.en: `Nonsense!' said Alice, very loudly and decidedly, and the Queen was silent.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 19 段）

paragraphs.en: The King laid his hand upon her arm, and timidly said `Consider, my dear: she is only a child!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 20 段）

paragraphs.en: The Queen turned angrily away from him, and said to the Knave `Turn them over!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 21 段）

paragraphs.en: The Knave did so, very carefully, with one foot.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 22 段）

paragraphs.en: `Get up!' said the Queen, in a shrill, loud voice, and the three gardeners instantly jumped up, and began bowing to the King, the Queen, the royal children, and everybody else.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 23 段）

paragraphs.en: `Leave off that!' screamed the Queen. `You make me giddy.' And then, turning to the rose-tree, she went on, `What HAVE you been doing here?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 24 段）

paragraphs.en: `May it please your Majesty,' said Two, in a very humble tone, going down on one knee as he spoke, `we were trying--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 25 段）

paragraphs.en: `I see!' said the Queen, who had meanwhile been examining the roses. `Off with their heads!' and the procession moved on, three of the soldiers remaining behind to execute the unfortunate gardeners, who ran to Alice for protection.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 26 段）

paragraphs.en: `You shan't be beheaded!' said Alice, and she put them into a large flower-pot that stood near. The three soldiers wandered about for a minute or two, looking for them, and then quietly marched off after the others.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 27 段）

paragraphs.en: `Are their heads off?' shouted the Queen.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 28 段）

paragraphs.en: `Their heads are gone, if it please your Majesty!' the soldiers shouted in reply.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 29 段）

paragraphs.en: `That's right!' shouted the Queen. `Can you play croquet?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 30 段）

paragraphs.en: The soldiers were silent, and looked at Alice, as the question was evidently meant for her.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 31 段）

paragraphs.en: `Yes!' shouted Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 32 段）

paragraphs.en: `Come on, then!' roared the Queen, and Alice joined the procession, wondering very much what would happen next.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 33 段）

paragraphs.en: `It's--it's a very fine day!' said a timid voice at her side. She was walking by the White Rabbit, who was peeping anxiously into her face.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 34 段）

paragraphs.en: `Very,' said Alice: `--where's the Duchess?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 35 段）

paragraphs.en: `Hush! Hush!' said the Rabbit in a low, hurried tone. He looked anxiously over his shoulder as he spoke, and then raised himself upon tiptoe, put his mouth close to her ear, and whispered `She's under sentence of execution.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 36 段）

paragraphs.en: `What for?' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 37 段）

paragraphs.en: `Did you say "What a pity!"?' the Rabbit asked.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 38 段）

paragraphs.en: `No, I didn't,' said Alice: `I don't think it's at all a pity. I said "What for?"'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 39 段）

paragraphs.en: `She boxed the Queen's ears--' the Rabbit began. Alice gave a little scream of laughter. `Oh, hush!' the Rabbit whispered in a frightened tone. `The Queen will hear you! You see, she came rather late, and the Queen said--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 40 段）

paragraphs.en: `Get to your places!' shouted the Queen in a voice of thunder, and people began running about in all directions, tumbling up against each other; however, they got settled down in a minute or two, and the game began. Alice thought she had never seen such a curious croquet-ground in her life; it was all ridges and furrows; the balls were live hedgehogs, the mallets live flamingoes, and the soldiers had to double themselves up and to stand on their hands and feet, to make the arches.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 41 段）

paragraphs.en: The chief difficulty Alice found at first was in managing her flamingo: she succeeded in getting its body tucked away, comfortably enough, under her arm, with its legs hanging down, but generally, just as she had got its neck nicely straightened out, and was going to give the hedgehog a blow with its head, it WOULD twist itself round and look up in her face, with such a puzzled expression that she could not help bursting out laughing: and when she had got its head down, and was going to begin again, it was very provoking to find that the hedgehog had unrolled itself, and was in the act of crawling away: besides all this, there was generally a ridge or furrow in the way wherever she wanted to send the hedgehog to, and, as the doubled-up soldiers were always getting up and walking off to other parts of the ground, Alice soon came to the conclusion that it was a very difficult game indeed.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 42 段）

paragraphs.en: The players all played at once without waiting for turns, quarrelling all the while, and fighting for the hedgehogs; and in a very short time the Queen was in a furious passion, and went stamping about, and shouting `Off with his head!' or `Off with her head!' about once in a minute.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 43 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice began to feel very uneasy: to be sure, she had not as yet had any dispute with the Queen, but she knew that it might happen any minute, `and then,' thought she, `what would become of me? They're dreadfully fond of beheading people here; the great wonder is, that there's any one left alive!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 44 段）

paragraphs.en: She was looking about for some way of escape, and wondering whether she could get away without being seen, when she noticed a curious appearance in the air: it puzzled her very much at first, but, after watching it a minute or two, she made it out to be a grin, and she said to herself `It's the Cheshire Cat: now I shall have somebody to talk to.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 45 段）

paragraphs.en: `How are you getting on?' said the Cat, as soon as there was mouth enough for it to speak with.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 46 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice waited till the eyes appeared, and then nodded. `It's no use speaking to it,' she thought, `till its ears have come, or at least one of them.' In another minute the whole head appeared, and then Alice put down her flamingo, and began an account of the game, feeling very glad she had someone to listen to her. The Cat seemed to think that there was enough of it now in sight, and no more of it appeared.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 47 段）

paragraphs.en: `I don't think they play at all fairly,' Alice began, in rather a complaining tone, `and they all quarrel so dreadfully one can't hear oneself speak--and they don't seem to have any rules in particular; at least, if there are, nobody attends to them--and you've no idea how confusing it is all the things being alive; for instance, there's the arch I've got to go through next walking about at the other end of the ground--and I should have croqueted the Queen's hedgehog just now, only it ran away when it saw mine coming!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 48 段）

paragraphs.en: `How do you like the Queen?' said the Cat in a low voice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 49 段）

paragraphs.en: `Not at all,' said Alice: `she's so extremely--' Just then she noticed that the Queen was close behind her, listening: so she went on, `--likely to win, that it's hardly worth while finishing the game.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 50 段）

paragraphs.en: The Queen smiled and passed on.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 51 段）

paragraphs.en: `Who ARE you talking to?' said the King, going up to Alice, and looking at the Cat's head with great curiosity.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 52 段）

paragraphs.en: `It's a friend of mine--a Cheshire Cat,' said Alice: `allow me to introduce it.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 53 段）

paragraphs.en: `I don't like the look of it at all,' said the King: `however, it may kiss my hand if it likes.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 54 段）

paragraphs.en: `I'd rather not,' the Cat remarked.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 55 段）

paragraphs.en: `Don't be impertinent,' said the King, `and don't look at me like that!' He got behind Alice as he spoke.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 56 段）

paragraphs.en: `A cat may look at a king,' said Alice. `I've read that in some book, but I don't remember where.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 57 段）

paragraphs.en: `Well, it must be removed,' said the King very decidedly, and he called the Queen, who was passing at the moment, `My dear! I wish you would have this cat removed!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 58 段）

paragraphs.en: The Queen had only one way of settling all difficulties, great or small. `Off with his head!' she said, without even looking round.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 59 段）

paragraphs.en: `I'll fetch the executioner myself,' said the King eagerly, and he hurried off.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 60 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice thought she might as well go back, and see how the game was going on, as she heard the Queen's voice in the distance, screaming with passion. She had already heard her sentence three of the players to be executed for having missed their turns, and she did not like the look of things at all, as the game was in such confusion that she never knew whether it was her turn or not. So she went in search of her hedgehog.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 61 段）

paragraphs.en: The hedgehog was engaged in a fight with another hedgehog, which seemed to Alice an excellent opportunity for croqueting one of them with the other: the only difficulty was, that her flamingo was gone across to the other side of the garden, where Alice could see it trying in a helpless sort of way to fly up into a tree.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 62 段）

paragraphs.en: By the time she had caught the flamingo and brought it back, the fight was over, and both the hedgehogs were out of sight: `but it doesn't matter much,' thought Alice, `as all the arches are gone from this side of the ground.' So she tucked it away under her arm, that it might not escape again, and went back for a little more conversation with her friend.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 63 段）

paragraphs.en: When she got back to the Cheshire Cat, she was surprised to find quite a large crowd collected round it: there was a dispute going on between the executioner, the King, and the Queen, who were all talking at once, while all the rest were quite silent, and looked very uncomfortable.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 64 段）

paragraphs.en: The moment Alice appeared, she was appealed to by all three to settle the question, and they repeated their arguments to her, though, as they all spoke at once, she found it very hard indeed to make out exactly what they said.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 65 段）

paragraphs.en: The executioner's argument was, that you couldn't cut off a head unless there was a body to cut it off from: that he had never had to do such a thing before, and he wasn't going to begin at HIS time of life.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 66 段）

paragraphs.en: The King's argument was, that anything that had a head could be beheaded, and that you weren't to talk nonsense.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 67 段）

paragraphs.en: The Queen's argument was, that if something wasn't done about it in less than no time she'd have everybody executed, all round. (It was this last remark that had made the whole party look so grave and anxious.)
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 68 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice could think of nothing else to say but `It belongs to the Duchess: you'd better ask HER about it.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 69 段）

paragraphs.en: `She's in prison,' the Queen said to the executioner: `fetch her here.' And the executioner went off like an arrow.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 70 段）

paragraphs.en: The Cat's head began fading away the moment he was gone, and, by the time he had come back with the Duchess, it had entirely disappeared; so the King and the executioner ran wildly up and down looking for it, while the rest of the party went back to the game.
paragraphs.zh: （第 8 章 · 王后的槌球场 第 71 段）

paragraphs.en:
CHAPTER IX
The Mock Turtle's Story
paragraphs.zh: 第九章 · 假海龟的故事
paragraphs.chapterTitleZh: 第九章 · 假海龟的故事

paragraphs.en: `You can't think how glad I am to see you again, you dear old thing!' said the Duchess, as she tucked her arm affectionately into Alice's, and they walked off together.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 1 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice was very glad to find her in such a pleasant temper, and thought to herself that perhaps it was only the pepper that had made her so savage when they met in the kitchen.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 2 段）

paragraphs.en: `When I'M a Duchess,' she said to herself, (not in a very hopeful tone though), `I won't have any pepper in my kitchen AT ALL. Soup does very well without--Maybe it's always pepper that makes people hot-tempered,' she went on, very much pleased at having found out a new kind of rule, `and vinegar that makes them sour--and camomile that makes them bitter--and--and barley-sugar and such things that make children sweet-tempered. I only wish people knew that: then they wouldn't be so stingy about it, you know--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 3 段）

paragraphs.en: She had quite forgotten the Duchess by this time, and was a little startled when she heard her voice close to her ear. `You're thinking about something, my dear, and that makes you forget to talk. I can't tell you just now what the moral of that is, but I shall remember it in a bit.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 4 段）

paragraphs.en: `Perhaps it hasn't one,' Alice ventured to remark.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 5 段）

paragraphs.en: `Tut, tut, child!' said the Duchess. `Everything's got a moral, if only you can find it.' And she squeezed herself up closer to Alice's side as she spoke.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 6 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice did not much like keeping so close to her: first, because the Duchess was VERY ugly; and secondly, because she was exactly the right height to rest her chin upon Alice's shoulder, and it was an uncomfortably sharp chin. However, she did not like to be rude, so she bore it as well as she could.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 7 段）

paragraphs.en: `The game's going on rather better now,' she said, by way of keeping up the conversation a little.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 8 段）

paragraphs.en: `'Tis so,' said the Duchess: `and the moral of that is--"Oh, 'tis love, 'tis love, that makes the world go round!"'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 9 段）

paragraphs.en: `Somebody said,' Alice whispered, `that it's done by everybody minding their own business!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 10 段）

paragraphs.en: `Ah, well! It means much the same thing,' said the Duchess, digging her sharp little chin into Alice's shoulder as she added, `and the moral of THAT is--"Take care of the sense, and the sounds will take care of themselves."'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 11 段）

paragraphs.en: `How fond she is of finding morals in things!' Alice thought to herself.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 12 段）

paragraphs.en: `I dare say you're wondering why I don't put my arm round your waist,' the Duchess said after a pause: `the reason is, that I'm doubtful about the temper of your flamingo. Shall I try the experiment?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 13 段）

paragraphs.en: `HE might bite,' Alice cautiously replied, not feeling at all anxious to have the experiment tried.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 14 段）

paragraphs.en: `Very true,' said the Duchess: `flamingoes and mustard both bite. And the moral of that is--"Birds of a feather flock together."'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 15 段）

paragraphs.en: `Only mustard isn't a bird,' Alice remarked.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 16 段）

paragraphs.en: `Right, as usual,' said the Duchess: `what a clear way you have of putting things!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 17 段）

paragraphs.en: `It's a mineral, I THINK,' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 18 段）

paragraphs.en: `Of course it is,' said the Duchess, who seemed ready to agree to everything that Alice said; `there's a large mustard-mine near here. And the moral of that is--"The more there is of mine, the less there is of yours."'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 19 段）

paragraphs.en: `Oh, I know!' exclaimed Alice, who had not attended to this last remark, `it's a vegetable. It doesn't look like one, but it is.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 20 段）

paragraphs.en: `I quite agree with you,' said the Duchess; `and the moral of that is--"Be what you would seem to be"--or if you'd like it put more simply--"Never imagine yourself not to be otherwise than what it might appear to others that what you were or might have been was not otherwise than what you had been would have appeared to them to be otherwise."'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 21 段）

paragraphs.en: `I think I should understand that better,' Alice said very politely, `if I had it written down: but I can't quite follow it as you say it.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 22 段）

paragraphs.en: `That's nothing to what I could say if I chose,' the Duchess replied, in a pleased tone.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 23 段）

paragraphs.en: `Pray don't trouble yourself to say it any longer than that,' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 24 段）

paragraphs.en: `Oh, don't talk about trouble!' said the Duchess. `I make you a present of everything I've said as yet.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 25 段）

paragraphs.en: `A cheap sort of present!' thought Alice. `I'm glad they don't give birthday presents like that!' But she did not venture to say it out loud.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 26 段）

paragraphs.en: `Thinking again?' the Duchess asked, with another dig of her sharp little chin.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 27 段）

paragraphs.en: `I've a right to think,' said Alice sharply, for she was beginning to feel a little worried.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 28 段）

paragraphs.en: `Just about as much right,' said the Duchess, `as pigs have to fly; and the m--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 29 段）

paragraphs.en: But here, to Alice's great surprise, the Duchess's voice died away, even in the middle of her favourite word `moral,' and the arm that was linked into hers began to tremble. Alice looked up, and there stood the Queen in front of them, with her arms folded, frowning like a thunderstorm.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 30 段）

paragraphs.en: `A fine day, your Majesty!' the Duchess began in a low, weak voice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 31 段）

paragraphs.en: `Now, I give you fair warning,' shouted the Queen, stamping on the ground as she spoke; `either you or your head must be off, and that in about half no time! Take your choice!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 32 段）

paragraphs.en: The Duchess took her choice, and was gone in a moment.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 33 段）

paragraphs.en: `Let's go on with the game,' the Queen said to Alice; and Alice was too much frightened to say a word, but slowly followed her back to the croquet-ground.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 34 段）

paragraphs.en: The other guests had taken advantage of the Queen's absence, and were resting in the shade: however, the moment they saw her, they hurried back to the game, the Queen merely remarking that a moment's delay would cost them their lives.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 35 段）

paragraphs.en: All the time they were playing the Queen never left off quarrelling with the other players, and shouting `Off with his head!' or `Off with her head!' Those whom she sentenced were taken into custody by the soldiers, who of course had to leave off being arches to do this, so that by the end of half an hour or so there were no arches left, and all the players, except the King, the Queen, and Alice, were in custody and under sentence of execution.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 36 段）

paragraphs.en: Then the Queen left off, quite out of breath, and said to Alice, `Have you seen the Mock Turtle yet?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 37 段）

paragraphs.en: `No,' said Alice. `I don't even know what a Mock Turtle is.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 38 段）

paragraphs.en: `It's the thing Mock Turtle Soup is made from,' said the Queen.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 39 段）

paragraphs.en: `I never saw one, or heard of one,' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 40 段）

paragraphs.en: `Come on, then,' said the Queen, `and he shall tell you his history,'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 41 段）

paragraphs.en: As they walked off together, Alice heard the King say in a low voice, to the company generally, `You are all pardoned.' `Come, THAT'S a good thing!' she said to herself, for she had felt quite unhappy at the number of executions the Queen had ordered.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 42 段）

paragraphs.en: They very soon came upon a Gryphon, lying fast asleep in the sun. (IF you don't know what a Gryphon is, look at the picture.) `Up, lazy thing!' said the Queen, `and take this young lady to see the Mock Turtle, and to hear his history. I must go back and see after some executions I have ordered'; and she walked off, leaving Alice alone with the Gryphon. Alice did not quite like the look of the creature, but on the whole she thought it would be quite as safe to stay with it as to go after that savage Queen: so she waited.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 43 段）

paragraphs.en: The Gryphon sat up and rubbed its eyes: then it watched the Queen till she was out of sight: then it chuckled. `What fun!' said the Gryphon, half to itself, half to Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 44 段）

paragraphs.en: `What IS the fun?' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 45 段）

paragraphs.en: `Why, SHE,' said the Gryphon. `It's all her fancy, that: they never executes nobody, you know. Come on!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 46 段）

paragraphs.en: `Everybody says "come on!" here,' thought Alice, as she went slowly after it: `I never was so ordered about in all my life, never!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 47 段）

paragraphs.en: They had not gone far before they saw the Mock Turtle in the distance, sitting sad and lonely on a little ledge of rock, and, as they came nearer, Alice could hear him sighing as if his heart would break. She pitied him deeply. `What is his sorrow?' she asked the Gryphon, and the Gryphon answered, very nearly in the same words as before, `It's all his fancy, that: he hasn't got no sorrow, you know. Come on!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 48 段）

paragraphs.en: So they went up to the Mock Turtle, who looked at them with large eyes full of tears, but said nothing.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 49 段）

paragraphs.en: `This here young lady,' said the Gryphon, `she wants for to know your history, she do.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 50 段）

paragraphs.en: `I'll tell it her,' said the Mock Turtle in a deep, hollow tone: `sit down, both of you, and don't speak a word till I've finished.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 51 段）

paragraphs.en: So they sat down, and nobody spoke for some minutes. Alice thought to herself, `I don't see how he can EVEN finish, if he doesn't begin.' But she waited patiently.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 52 段）

paragraphs.en: `Once,' said the Mock Turtle at last, with a deep sigh, `I was a real Turtle.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 53 段）

paragraphs.en: These words were followed by a very long silence, broken only by an occasional exclamation of `Hjckrrh!' from the Gryphon, and the constant heavy sobbing of the Mock Turtle. Alice was very nearly getting up and saying, `Thank you, sir, for your interesting story,' but she could not help thinking there MUST be more to come, so she sat still and said nothing.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 54 段）

paragraphs.en: `When we were little,' the Mock Turtle went on at last, more calmly, though still sobbing a little now and then, `we went to school in the sea. The master was an old Turtle--we used to call him Tortoise--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 55 段）

paragraphs.en: `Why did you call him Tortoise, if he wasn't one?' Alice asked.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 56 段）

paragraphs.en: `We called him Tortoise because he taught us,' said the Mock Turtle angrily: `really you are very dull!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 57 段）

paragraphs.en: `You ought to be ashamed of yourself for asking such a simple question,' added the Gryphon; and then they both sat silent and looked at poor Alice, who felt ready to sink into the earth. At last the Gryphon said to the Mock Turtle, `Drive on, old fellow! Don't be all day about it!' and he went on in these words:
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 58 段）

paragraphs.en: `Yes, we went to school in the sea, though you mayn't believe it--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 59 段）

paragraphs.en: `I never said I didn't!' interrupted Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 60 段）

paragraphs.en: `You did,' said the Mock Turtle.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 61 段）

paragraphs.en: `Hold your tongue!' added the Gryphon, before Alice could speak again. The Mock Turtle went on.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 62 段）

paragraphs.en: `We had the best of educations--in fact, we went to school every day--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 63 段）

paragraphs.en: `I'VE been to a day-school, too,' said Alice; `you needn't be so proud as all that.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 64 段）

paragraphs.en: `With extras?' asked the Mock Turtle a little anxiously.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 65 段）

paragraphs.en: `Yes,' said Alice, `we learned French and music.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 66 段）

paragraphs.en: `And washing?' said the Mock Turtle.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 67 段）

paragraphs.en: `Certainly not!' said Alice indignantly.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 68 段）

paragraphs.en: `Ah! then yours wasn't a really good school,' said the Mock Turtle in a tone of great relief. `Now at OURS they had at the end of the bill, "French, music, AND WASHING--extra."'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 69 段）

paragraphs.en: `You couldn't have wanted it much,' said Alice; `living at the bottom of the sea.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 70 段）

paragraphs.en: `I couldn't afford to learn it.' said the Mock Turtle with a sigh. `I only took the regular course.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 71 段）

paragraphs.en: `What was that?' inquired Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 72 段）

paragraphs.en: `Reeling and Writhing, of course, to begin with,' the Mock Turtle replied; `and then the different branches of Arithmetic-- Ambition, Distraction, Uglification, and Derision.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 73 段）

paragraphs.en: `I never heard of "Uglification,"' Alice ventured to say. `What is it?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 74 段）

paragraphs.en: The Gryphon lifted up both its paws in surprise. `What! Never heard of uglifying!' it exclaimed. `You know what to beautify is, I suppose?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 75 段）

paragraphs.en: `Yes,' said Alice doubtfully: `it means--to--make--anything--prettier.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 76 段）

paragraphs.en: `Well, then,' the Gryphon went on, `if you don't know what to uglify is, you ARE a simpleton.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 77 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice did not feel encouraged to ask any more questions about it, so she turned to the Mock Turtle, and said `What else had you to learn?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 78 段）

paragraphs.en: `Well, there was Mystery,' the Mock Turtle replied, counting off the subjects on his flappers, `--Mystery, ancient and modern, with Seaography: then Drawling--the Drawling-master was an old conger-eel, that used to come once a week: HE taught us Drawling, Stretching, and Fainting in Coils.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 79 段）

paragraphs.en: `What was THAT like?' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 80 段）

paragraphs.en: `Well, I can't show it you myself,' the Mock Turtle said: `I'm too stiff. And the Gryphon never learnt it.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 81 段）

paragraphs.en: `Hadn't time,' said the Gryphon: `I went to the Classics master, though. He was an old crab, HE was.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 82 段）

paragraphs.en: `I never went to him,' the Mock Turtle said with a sigh: `he taught Laughing and Grief, they used to say.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 83 段）

paragraphs.en: `So he did, so he did,' said the Gryphon, sighing in his turn; and both creatures hid their faces in their paws.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 84 段）

paragraphs.en: `And how many hours a day did you do lessons?' said Alice, in a hurry to change the subject.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 85 段）

paragraphs.en: `Ten hours the first day,' said the Mock Turtle: `nine the next, and so on.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 86 段）

paragraphs.en: `What a curious plan!' exclaimed Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 87 段）

paragraphs.en: `That's the reason they're called lessons,' the Gryphon remarked: `because they lessen from day to day.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 88 段）

paragraphs.en: This was quite a new idea to Alice, and she thought it over a little before she made her next remark. `Then the eleventh day must have been a holiday?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 89 段）

paragraphs.en: `Of course it was,' said the Mock Turtle.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 90 段）

paragraphs.en: `And how did you manage on the twelfth?' Alice went on eagerly.
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 91 段）

paragraphs.en: `That's enough about lessons,' the Gryphon interrupted in a very decided tone: `tell her something about the games now.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 9 章 · 假海龟的故事 第 92 段）

paragraphs.en:
CHAPTER X
The Lobster Quadrille
paragraphs.zh: 第十章 · 龙虾对舞

paragraphs.en: The Mock Turtle sighed deeply, and drew the back of one flapper across his eyes. He looked at Alice, and tried to speak, but for a minute or two sobs choked his voice. `Same as if he had a bone in his throat,' said the Gryphon: and it set to work shaking him and punching him in the back. At last the Mock Turtle recovered his voice, and, with tears running down his cheeks, he went on again:--
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 1 段）

paragraphs.en: `You may not have lived much under the sea--' (`I haven't,' said Alice)-- `and perhaps you were never even introduced to a lobster--' (Alice began to say `I once tasted--' but checked herself hastily, and said `No, never') `--so you can have no idea what a delightful thing a Lobster Quadrille is!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 2 段）

paragraphs.en: `No, indeed,' said Alice. `What sort of a dance is it?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 3 段）

paragraphs.en: `Why,' said the Gryphon, `you first form into a line along the sea-shore--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 4 段）

paragraphs.en: `Two lines!' cried the Mock Turtle. `Seals, turtles, salmon, and so on; then, when you've cleared all the jelly-fish out of the way--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 5 段）

paragraphs.en: `THAT generally takes some time,' interrupted the Gryphon.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 6 段）

paragraphs.en: `--you advance twice--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 7 段）

paragraphs.en: `Each with a lobster as a partner!' cried the Gryphon.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 8 段）

paragraphs.en: `Of course,' the Mock Turtle said: `advance twice, set to partners--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 9 段）

paragraphs.en: `--change lobsters, and retire in same order,' continued the Gryphon.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 10 段）

paragraphs.en: `Then, you know,' the Mock Turtle went on, `you throw the--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 11 段）

paragraphs.en: `The lobsters!' shouted the Gryphon, with a bound into the air.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 12 段）

paragraphs.en: `--as far out to sea as you can--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 13 段）

paragraphs.en: `Swim after them!' screamed the Gryphon.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 14 段）

paragraphs.en: `Turn a somersault in the sea!' cried the Mock Turtle, capering wildly about.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 15 段）

paragraphs.en: `Change lobsters again!' yelled the Gryphon at the top of its voice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 16 段）

paragraphs.en: `Back to land again, and that's all the first figure,' said the Mock Turtle, suddenly dropping his voice; and the two creatures, who had been jumping about like mad things all this time, sat down again very sadly and quietly, and looked at Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 17 段）

paragraphs.en: `It must be a very pretty dance,' said Alice timidly.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 18 段）

paragraphs.en: `Would you like to see a little of it?' said the Mock Turtle.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 19 段）

paragraphs.en: `Very much indeed,' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 20 段）

paragraphs.en: `Come, let's try the first figure!' said the Mock Turtle to the Gryphon. `We can do without lobsters, you know. Which shall sing?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 21 段）

paragraphs.en: `Oh, YOU sing,' said the Gryphon. `I've forgotten the words.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 22 段）

paragraphs.en: So they began solemnly dancing round and round Alice, every now and then treading on her toes when they passed too close, and waving their forepaws to mark the time, while the Mock Turtle sang this, very slowly and sadly:--
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 23 段）

paragraphs.en: `"Will you walk a little faster?" said a whiting to a snail. "There's a porpoise close behind us, and he's treading on my tail. See how eagerly the lobsters and the turtles all advance! They are waiting on the shingle--will you come and join the dance?
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 24 段）

paragraphs.en: Will you, won't you, will you, won't you, will you join the dance? Will you, won't you, will you, won't you, won't you join the dance?
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 25 段）

paragraphs.en: "You can really have no notion how delightful it will be When they take us up and throw us, with the lobsters, out to sea!" But the snail replied "Too far, too far!" and gave a look askance-- Said he thanked the whiting kindly, but he would not join the dance. Would not, could not, would not, could not, would not join the dance. Would not, could not, would not, could not, could not join the dance.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 26 段）

paragraphs.en: `"What matters it how far we go?" his scaly friend replied. "There is another shore, you know, upon the other side. The further off from England the nearer is to France-- Then turn not pale, beloved snail, but come and join the dance.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 27 段）

paragraphs.en: Will you, won't you, will you, won't you, will you join the dance? Will you, won't you, will you, won't you, won't you join the dance?"'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 28 段）

paragraphs.en: `Thank you, it's a very interesting dance to watch,' said Alice, feeling very glad that it was over at last: `and I do so like that curious song about the whiting!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 29 段）

paragraphs.en: `Oh, as to the whiting,' said the Mock Turtle, `they--you've seen them, of course?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 30 段）

paragraphs.en: `Yes,' said Alice, `I've often seen them at dinn--' she checked herself hastily.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 31 段）

paragraphs.en: `I don't know where Dinn may be,' said the Mock Turtle, `but if you've seen them so often, of course you know what they're like.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 32 段）

paragraphs.en: `I believe so,' Alice replied thoughtfully. `They have their tails in their mouths--and they're all over crumbs.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 33 段）

paragraphs.en: `You're wrong about the crumbs,' said the Mock Turtle: `crumbs would all wash off in the sea. But they HAVE their tails in their mouths; and the reason is--' here the Mock Turtle yawned and shut his eyes.--`Tell her about the reason and all that,' he said to the Gryphon.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 34 段）

paragraphs.en: `The reason is,' said the Gryphon, `that they WOULD go with the lobsters to the dance. So they got thrown out to sea. So they had to fall a long way. So they got their tails fast in their mouths. So they couldn't get them out again. That's all.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 35 段）

paragraphs.en: `Thank you,' said Alice, `it's very interesting. I never knew so much about a whiting before.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 36 段）

paragraphs.en: `I can tell you more than that, if you like,' said the Gryphon. `Do you know why it's called a whiting?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 37 段）

paragraphs.en: `I never thought about it,' said Alice. `Why?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 38 段）

paragraphs.en: `IT DOES THE BOOTS AND SHOES.' the Gryphon replied very solemnly.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 39 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice was thoroughly puzzled. `Does the boots and shoes!' she repeated in a wondering tone.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 40 段）

paragraphs.en: `Why, what are YOUR shoes done with?' said the Gryphon. `I mean, what makes them so shiny?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 41 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice looked down at them, and considered a little before she gave her answer. `They're done with blacking, I believe.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 42 段）

paragraphs.en: `Boots and shoes under the sea,' the Gryphon went on in a deep voice, `are done with a whiting. Now you know.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 43 段）

paragraphs.en: `And what are they made of?' Alice asked in a tone of great curiosity.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 44 段）

paragraphs.en: `Soles and eels, of course,' the Gryphon replied rather impatiently: `any shrimp could have told you that.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 45 段）

paragraphs.en: `If I'd been the whiting,' said Alice, whose thoughts were still running on the song, `I'd have said to the porpoise, "Keep back, please: we don't want YOU with us!"'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 46 段）

paragraphs.en: `They were obliged to have him with them,' the Mock Turtle said: `no wise fish would go anywhere without a porpoise.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 47 段）

paragraphs.en: `Wouldn't it really?' said Alice in a tone of great surprise.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 48 段）

paragraphs.en: `Of course not,' said the Mock Turtle: `why, if a fish came to ME, and told me he was going a journey, I should say "With what porpoise?"'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 49 段）

paragraphs.en: `Don't you mean "purpose"?' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 50 段）

paragraphs.en: `I mean what I say,' the Mock Turtle replied in an offended tone. And the Gryphon added `Come, let's hear some of YOUR adventures.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 51 段）

paragraphs.en: `I could tell you my adventures--beginning from this morning,' said Alice a little timidly: `but it's no use going back to yesterday, because I was a different person then.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 52 段）

paragraphs.en: `Explain all that,' said the Mock Turtle.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 53 段）

paragraphs.en: `No, no! The adventures first,' said the Gryphon in an impatient tone: `explanations take such a dreadful time.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 54 段）

paragraphs.en: So Alice began telling them her adventures from the time when she first saw the White Rabbit. She was a little nervous about it just at first, the two creatures got so close to her, one on each side, and opened their eyes and mouths so VERY wide, but she gained courage as she went on. Her listeners were perfectly quiet till she got to the part about her repeating `YOU ARE OLD, FATHER WILLIAM,' to the Caterpillar, and the words all coming different, and then the Mock Turtle drew a long breath, and said `That's very curious.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 55 段）

paragraphs.en: `It's all about as curious as it can be,' said the Gryphon.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 56 段）

paragraphs.en: `It all came different!' the Mock Turtle repeated thoughtfully. `I should like to hear her try and repeat something now. Tell her to begin.' He looked at the Gryphon as if he thought it had some kind of authority over Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 57 段）

paragraphs.en: `Stand up and repeat "'TIS THE VOICE OF THE SLUGGARD,"' said the Gryphon.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 58 段）

paragraphs.en: `How the creatures order one about, and make one repeat lessons!' thought Alice; `I might as well be at school at once.' However, she got up, and began to repeat it, but her head was so saying, and the words came very queer indeed:--
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 59 段）

paragraphs.en: `'Tis the voice of the Lobster; I heard him declare, "You have baked me too brown, I must sugar my hair." As a duck with its eyelids, so he with his nose Trims his belt and his buttons, and turns out his toes.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 60 段）

paragraphs.en: [later editions continued as follows When the sands are all dry, he is gay as a lark, And will talk in contemptuous tones of the Shark, But, when the tide rises and sharks are around, His voice has a timid and tremulous sound.]
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 61 段）

paragraphs.en: `That's different from what I used to say when I was a child,' said the Gryphon.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 62 段）

paragraphs.en: `Well, I never heard it before,' said the Mock Turtle; `but it sounds uncommon nonsense.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 63 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice said nothing; she had sat down with her face in her hands, wondering if anything would EVER happen in a natural way again.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 64 段）

paragraphs.en: `I should like to have it explained,' said the Mock Turtle.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 65 段）

paragraphs.en: `She can't explain it,' said the Gryphon hastily. `Go on with the next verse.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 66 段）

paragraphs.en: `But about his toes?' the Mock Turtle persisted. `How COULD he turn them out with his nose, you know?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 67 段）

paragraphs.en: `It's the first position in dancing.' Alice said; but was dreadfully puzzled by the whole thing, and longed to change the subject.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 68 段）

paragraphs.en: `Go on with the next verse,' the Gryphon repeated impatiently: `it begins "I passed by his garden."'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 69 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice did not dare to disobey, though she felt sure it would all come wrong, and she went on in a trembling voice:--
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 70 段）

paragraphs.en: `I passed by his garden, and marked, with one eye, How the Owl and the Panther were sharing a pie--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 71 段）

paragraphs.en: [later editions continued as follows The Panther took pie-crust, and gravy, and meat, While the Owl had the dish as its share of the treat. When the pie was all finished, the Owl, as a boon, Was kindly permitted to pocket the spoon: While the Panther received knife and fork with a growl, And concluded the banquet--]
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 72 段）

paragraphs.en: `What IS the use of repeating all that stuff,' the Mock Turtle interrupted, `if you don't explain it as you go on? It's by far the most confusing thing I ever heard!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 73 段）

paragraphs.en: `Yes, I think you'd better leave off,' said the Gryphon: and Alice was only too glad to do so.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 74 段）

paragraphs.en: Gryphon went on. `Or would you like the Mock Turtle to sing you a song?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 75 段）

paragraphs.en: `Oh, a song, please, if the Mock Turtle would be so kind,' Alice replied, so eagerly that the Gryphon said, in a rather offended tone, `Hm! No accounting for tastes! Sing her "Turtle Soup," will you, old fellow?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 76 段）

paragraphs.en: The Mock Turtle sighed deeply, and began, in a voice sometimes choked with sobs, to sing this:--
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 77 段）

paragraphs.en: `Beautiful Soup, so rich and green, Waiting in a hot tureen! Who for such dainties would not stoop? Soup of the evening, beautiful Soup! Soup of the evening, beautiful Soup! Beau--ootiful Soo--oop! Beau--ootiful Soo--oop! Soo--oop of the e--e--evening, Beautiful, beautiful Soup!
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 78 段）

paragraphs.en: `Beautiful Soup! Who cares for fish, Game, or any other dish? Who would not give all else for two Pennyworth only of beautiful Soup? Pennyworth only of beautiful Soup? Beau--ootiful Soo--oop! Beau--ootiful Soo--oop! Soo--oop of the e--e--evening, Beautiful, beauti--FUL SOUP!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 79 段）

paragraphs.en: `Chorus again!' cried the Gryphon, and the Mock Turtle had just begun to repeat it, when a cry of `The trial's beginning!' was heard in the distance.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 80 段）

paragraphs.en: `Come on!' cried the Gryphon, and, taking Alice by the hand, it hurried off, without waiting for the end of the song.
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 81 段）

paragraphs.en: `What trial is it?' Alice panted as she ran; but the Gryphon only answered `Come on!' and ran the faster, while more and more faintly came, carried on the breeze that followed them, the melancholy words:--
