paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 82 段）

paragraphs.en: `Soo--oop of the e--e--evening, Beautiful, beautiful Soup!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 10 章 · 龙虾对舞 第 83 段）

paragraphs.en:
CHAPTER XI
Who Stole the Tarts?
paragraphs.zh: 第十一章 · 谁偷了馅饼？
paragraphs.chapterTitleZh: 第十一章 · 谁偷了馅饼？

paragraphs.en: The King and Queen of Hearts were seated on their throne when they arrived, with a great crowd assembled about them--all sorts of little birds and beasts, as well as the whole pack of cards: the Knave was standing before them, in chains, with a soldier on each side to guard him; and near the King was the White Rabbit, with a trumpet in one hand, and a scroll of parchment in the other. In the very middle of the court was a table, with a large dish of tarts upon it: they looked so good, that it made Alice quite hungry to look at them--`I wish they'd get the trial done,' she thought, `and hand round the refreshments!' But there seemed to be no chance of this, so she began looking at everything about her, to pass away the time.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 1 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice had never been in a court of justice before, but she had read about them in books, and she was quite pleased to find that she knew the name of nearly everything there. `That's the judge,' she said to herself, `because of his great wig.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 2 段）

paragraphs.en: The judge, by the way, was the King; and as he wore his crown over the wig, (look at the frontispiece if you want to see how he did it,) he did not look at all comfortable, and it was certainly not becoming.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 3 段）

paragraphs.en: `And that's the jury-box,' thought Alice, `and those twelve creatures,' (she was obliged to say `creatures,' you see, because some of them were animals, and some were birds,) `I suppose they are the jurors.' She said this last word two or three times over to herself, being rather proud of it: for she thought, and rightly too, that very few little girls of her age knew the meaning of it at all. However, `jury-men' would have done just as well.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 4 段）

paragraphs.en: The twelve jurors were all writing very busily on slates. `What are they doing?' Alice whispered to the Gryphon. `They can't have anything to put down yet, before the trial's begun.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 5 段）

paragraphs.en: `They're putting down their names,' the Gryphon whispered in reply, `for fear they should forget them before the end of the trial.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 6 段）

paragraphs.en: `Stupid things!' Alice began in a loud, indignant voice, but she stopped hastily, for the White Rabbit cried out, `Silence in the court!' and the King put on his spectacles and looked anxiously round, to make out who was talking.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 7 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice could see, as well as if she were looking over their shoulders, that all the jurors were writing down `stupid things!' on their slates, and she could even make out that one of them didn't know how to spell `stupid,' and that he had to ask his neighbour to tell him. `A nice muddle their slates'll be in before the trial's over!' thought Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 8 段）

paragraphs.en: One of the jurors had a pencil that squeaked. This of course, Alice could not stand, and she went round the court and got behind him, and very soon found an opportunity of taking it away. She did it so quickly that the poor little juror (it was Bill, the Lizard) could not make out at all what had become of it; so, after hunting all about for it, he was obliged to write with one finger for the rest of the day; and this was of very little use, as it left no mark on the slate.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 9 段）

paragraphs.en: `Herald, read the accusation!' said the King.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 10 段）

paragraphs.en: On this the White Rabbit blew three blasts on the trumpet, and then unrolled the parchment scroll, and read as follows:--
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 11 段）

paragraphs.en: `The Queen of Hearts, she made some tarts, All on a summer day: The Knave of Hearts, he stole those tarts, And took them quite away!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 12 段）

paragraphs.en: `Consider your verdict,' the King said to the jury.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 13 段）

paragraphs.en: `Not yet, not yet!' the Rabbit hastily interrupted. `There's a great deal to come before that!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 14 段）

paragraphs.en: `Call the first witness,' said the King; and the White Rabbit blew three blasts on the trumpet, and called out, `First witness!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 15 段）

paragraphs.en: The first witness was the Hatter. He came in with a teacup in one hand and a piece of bread-and-butter in the other. `I beg pardon, your Majesty,' he began, `for bringing these in: but I hadn't quite finished my tea when I was sent for.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 16 段）

paragraphs.en: `You ought to have finished,' said the King. `When did you begin?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 17 段）

paragraphs.en: The Hatter looked at the March Hare, who had followed him into the court, arm-in-arm with the Dormouse. `Fourteenth of March, I think it was,' he said.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 18 段）

paragraphs.en: `Fifteenth,' said the March Hare.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 19 段）

paragraphs.en: `Sixteenth,' added the Dormouse.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 20 段）

paragraphs.en: `Write that down,' the King said to the jury, and the jury eagerly wrote down all three dates on their slates, and then added them up, and reduced the answer to shillings and pence.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 21 段）

paragraphs.en: `Take off your hat,' the King said to the Hatter.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 22 段）

paragraphs.en: `It isn't mine,' said the Hatter.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 23 段）

paragraphs.en: `Stolen!' the King exclaimed, turning to the jury, who instantly made a memorandum of the fact.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 24 段）

paragraphs.en: `I keep them to sell,' the Hatter added as an explanation; `I've none of my own. I'm a hatter.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 25 段）

paragraphs.en: Here the Queen put on her spectacles, and began staring at the Hatter, who turned pale and fidgeted.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 26 段）

paragraphs.en: `Give your evidence,' said the King; `and don't be nervous, or I'll have you executed on the spot.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 27 段）

paragraphs.en: This did not seem to encourage the witness at all: he kept shifting from one foot to the other, looking uneasily at the Queen, and in his confusion he bit a large piece out of his teacup instead of the bread-and-butter.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 28 段）

paragraphs.en: Just at this moment Alice felt a very curious sensation, which puzzled her a good deal until she made out what it was: she was beginning to grow larger again, and she thought at first she would get up and leave the court; but on second thoughts she decided to remain where she was as long as there was room for her.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 29 段）

paragraphs.en: `I wish you wouldn't squeeze so.' said the Dormouse, who was sitting next to her. `I can hardly breathe.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 30 段）

paragraphs.en: `I can't help it,' said Alice very meekly: `I'm growing.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 31 段）

paragraphs.en: `You've no right to grow here,' said the Dormouse.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 32 段）

paragraphs.en: `Don't talk nonsense,' said Alice more boldly: `you know you're growing too.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 33 段）

paragraphs.en: `Yes, but I grow at a reasonable pace,' said the Dormouse: `not in that ridiculous fashion.' And he got up very sulkily and crossed over to the other side of the court.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 34 段）

paragraphs.en: All this time the Queen had never left off staring at the Hatter, and, just as the Dormouse crossed the court, she said to one of the officers of the court, `Bring me the list of the singers in the last concert!' on which the wretched Hatter trembled so, that he shook both his shoes off.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 35 段）

paragraphs.en: `Give your evidence,' the King repeated angrily, `or I'll have you executed, whether you're nervous or not.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 36 段）

paragraphs.en: `I'm a poor man, your Majesty,' the Hatter began, in a trembling voice, `--and I hadn't begun my tea--not above a week or so--and what with the bread-and-butter getting so thin--and the twinkling of the tea--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 37 段）

paragraphs.en: `The twinkling of the what?' said the King.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 38 段）

paragraphs.en: `It began with the tea,' the Hatter replied.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 39 段）

paragraphs.en: `Of course twinkling begins with a T!' said the King sharply. `Do you take me for a dunce? Go on!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 40 段）

paragraphs.en: `I'm a poor man,' the Hatter went on, `and most things twinkled after that--only the March Hare said--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 41 段）

paragraphs.en: `I didn't!' the March Hare interrupted in a great hurry.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 42 段）

paragraphs.en: `You did!' said the Hatter.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 43 段）

paragraphs.en: `I deny it!' said the March Hare.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 44 段）

paragraphs.en: `He denies it,' said the King: `leave out that part.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 45 段）

paragraphs.en: `Well, at any rate, the Dormouse said--' the Hatter went on, looking anxiously round to see if he would deny it too: but the Dormouse denied nothing, being fast asleep.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 46 段）

paragraphs.en: `After that,' continued the Hatter, `I cut some more bread- and-butter--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 47 段）

paragraphs.en: `But what did the Dormouse say?' one of the jury asked.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 48 段）

paragraphs.en: `That I can't remember,' said the Hatter.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 49 段）

paragraphs.en: `You MUST remember,' remarked the King, `or I'll have you executed.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 50 段）

paragraphs.en: The miserable Hatter dropped his teacup and bread-and-butter, and went down on one knee. `I'm a poor man, your Majesty,' he began.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 51 段）

paragraphs.en: `You're a very poor speaker,' said the King.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 52 段）

paragraphs.en: Here one of the guinea-pigs cheered, and was immediately suppressed by the officers of the court. (As that is rather a hard word, I will just explain to you how it was done. They had a large canvas bag, which tied up at the mouth with strings: into this they slipped the guinea-pig, head first, and then sat upon it.)
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 53 段）

paragraphs.en: `I'm glad I've seen that done,' thought Alice. `I've so often read in the newspapers, at the end of trials, "There was some attempts at applause, which was immediately suppressed by the officers of the court," and I never understood what it meant till now.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 54 段）

paragraphs.en: `If that's all you know about it, you may stand down,' continued the King.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 55 段）

paragraphs.en: `I can't go no lower,' said the Hatter: `I'm on the floor, as it is.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 56 段）

paragraphs.en: `Then you may SIT down,' the King replied.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 57 段）

paragraphs.en: Here the other guinea-pig cheered, and was suppressed.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 58 段）

paragraphs.en: `Come, that finished the guinea-pigs!' thought Alice. `Now we shall get on better.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 59 段）

paragraphs.en: `I'd rather finish my tea,' said the Hatter, with an anxious look at the Queen, who was reading the list of singers.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 60 段）

paragraphs.en: `You may go,' said the King, and the Hatter hurriedly left the court, without even waiting to put his shoes on.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 61 段）

paragraphs.en: `--and just take his head off outside,' the Queen added to one of the officers: but the Hatter was out of sight before the officer could get to the door.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 62 段）

paragraphs.en: `Call the next witness!' said the King.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 63 段）

paragraphs.en: The next witness was the Duchess's cook. She carried the pepper-box in her hand, and Alice guessed who it was, even before she got into the court, by the way the people near the door began sneezing all at once.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 64 段）

paragraphs.en: `Give your evidence,' said the King.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 65 段）

paragraphs.en: `Shan't,' said the cook.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 66 段）

paragraphs.en: The King looked anxiously at the White Rabbit, who said in a low voice, `Your Majesty must cross-examine THIS witness.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 67 段）

paragraphs.en: `Well, if I must, I must,' the King said, with a melancholy air, and, after folding his arms and frowning at the cook till his eyes were nearly out of sight, he said in a deep voice, `What are tarts made of?'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 68 段）

paragraphs.en: `Pepper, mostly,' said the cook.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 69 段）

paragraphs.en: `Treacle,' said a sleepy voice behind her.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 70 段）

paragraphs.en: `Collar that Dormouse,' the Queen shrieked out. `Behead that Dormouse! Turn that Dormouse out of court! Suppress him! Pinch him! Off with his whiskers!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 71 段）

paragraphs.en: For some minutes the whole court was in confusion, getting the Dormouse turned out, and, by the time they had settled down again, the cook had disappeared.
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 72 段）

paragraphs.en: `Never mind!' said the King, with an air of great relief. `Call the next witness.' And he added in an undertone to the Queen, `Really, my dear, YOU must cross-examine the next witness. It quite makes my forehead ache!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 73 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice watched the White Rabbit as he fumbled over the list, feeling very curious to see what the next witness would be like, `--for they haven't got much evidence YET,' she said to herself. Imagine her surprise, when the White Rabbit read out, at the top of his shrill little voice, the name `Alice!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 11 章 · 谁偷了馅饼？ 第 74 段）

paragraphs.en:
CHAPTER XII
Alice's Evidence
paragraphs.zh: 第十二章 · 爱丽丝的证词
paragraphs.chapterTitleZh: 第十二章 · 爱丽丝的证词

paragraphs.en: `Here!' cried Alice, quite forgetting in the flurry of the moment how large she had grown in the last few minutes, and she jumped up in such a hurry that she tipped over the jury-box with the edge of her skirt, upsetting all the jurymen on to the heads of the crowd below, and there they lay sprawling about, reminding her very much of a globe of goldfish she had accidentally upset the week before.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 1 段）

paragraphs.en: `Oh, I BEG your pardon!' she exclaimed in a tone of great dismay, and began picking them up again as quickly as she could, for the accident of the goldfish kept running in her head, and she had a vague sort of idea that they must be collected at once and put back into the jury-box, or they would die.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 2 段）

paragraphs.en: `The trial cannot proceed,' said the King in a very grave voice, `until all the jurymen are back in their proper places-- ALL,' he repeated with great emphasis, looking hard at Alice as he said do.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 3 段）

paragraphs.en: Alice looked at the jury-box, and saw that, in her haste, she had put the Lizard in head downwards, and the poor little thing was waving its tail about in a melancholy way, being quite unable to move. She soon got it out again, and put it right; `not that it signifies much,' she said to herself; `I should think it would be QUITE as much use in the trial one way up as the other.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 4 段）

paragraphs.en: As soon as the jury had a little recovered from the shock of being upset, and their slates and pencils had been found and handed back to them, they set to work very diligently to write out a history of the accident, all except the Lizard, who seemed too much overcome to do anything but sit with its mouth open, gazing up into the roof of the court.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 5 段）

paragraphs.en: `What do you know about this business?' the King said to Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 6 段）

paragraphs.en: `Nothing,' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 7 段）

paragraphs.en: `Nothing WHATEVER?' persisted the King.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 8 段）

paragraphs.en: `Nothing whatever,' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 9 段）

paragraphs.en: `That's very important,' the King said, turning to the jury. They were just beginning to write this down on their slates, when the White Rabbit interrupted: `UNimportant, your Majesty means, of course,' he said in a very respectful tone, but frowning and making faces at him as he spoke.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 10 段）

paragraphs.en: `UNimportant, of course, I meant,' the King hastily said, and went on to himself in an undertone, `important--unimportant-- unimportant--important--' as if he were trying which word sounded best.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 11 段）

paragraphs.en: Some of the jury wrote it down `important,' and some `unimportant.' Alice could see this, as she was near enough to look over their slates; `but it doesn't matter a bit,' she thought to herself.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 12 段）

paragraphs.en: At this moment the King, who had been for some time busily writing in his note-book, cackled out `Silence!' and read out from his book, `Rule Forty-two. ALL PERSONS MORE THAN A MILE HIGH TO LEAVE THE COURT.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 13 段）

paragraphs.en: Everybody looked at Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 14 段）

paragraphs.en: `I'M not a mile high,' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 15 段）

paragraphs.en: `You are,' said the King.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 16 段）

paragraphs.en: `Nearly two miles high,' added the Queen.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 17 段）

paragraphs.en: `Well, I shan't go, at any rate,' said Alice: `besides, that's not a regular rule: you invented it just now.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 18 段）

paragraphs.en: `It's the oldest rule in the book,' said the King.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 19 段）

paragraphs.en: `Then it ought to be Number One,' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 20 段）

paragraphs.en: The King turned pale, and shut his note-book hastily. `Consider your verdict,' he said to the jury, in a low, trembling voice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 21 段）

paragraphs.en: `There's more evidence to come yet, please your Majesty,' said the White Rabbit, jumping up in a great hurry; `this paper has just been picked up.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 22 段）

paragraphs.en: `What's in it?' said the Queen.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 23 段）

paragraphs.en: `I haven't opened it yet,' said the White Rabbit, `but it seems to be a letter, written by the prisoner to--to somebody.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 24 段）

paragraphs.en: `It must have been that,' said the King, `unless it was written to nobody, which isn't usual, you know.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 25 段）

paragraphs.en: `Who is it directed to?' said one of the jurymen.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 26 段）

paragraphs.en: `It isn't directed at all,' said the White Rabbit; `in fact, there's nothing written on the OUTSIDE.' He unfolded the paper as he spoke, and added `It isn't a letter, after all: it's a set of verses.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 27 段）

paragraphs.en: `Are they in the prisoner's handwriting?' asked another of the jurymen.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 28 段）

paragraphs.en: `No, they're not,' said the White Rabbit, `and that's the queerest thing about it.' (The jury all looked puzzled.)
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 29 段）

paragraphs.en: `He must have imitated somebody else's hand,' said the King. (The jury all brightened up again.)
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 30 段）

paragraphs.en: `Please your Majesty,' said the Knave, `I didn't write it, and they can't prove I did: there's no name signed at the end.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 31 段）

paragraphs.en: `If you didn't sign it,' said the King, `that only makes the matter worse. You MUST have meant some mischief, or else you'd have signed your name like an honest man.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 32 段）

paragraphs.en: There was a general clapping of hands at this: it was the first really clever thing the King had said that day.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 33 段）

paragraphs.en: `That PROVES his guilt,' said the Queen.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 34 段）

paragraphs.en: `It proves nothing of the sort!' said Alice. `Why, you don't even know what they're about!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 35 段）

paragraphs.en: `Read them,' said the King.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 36 段）

paragraphs.en: The White Rabbit put on his spectacles. `Where shall I begin, please your Majesty?' he asked.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 37 段）

paragraphs.en: `Begin at the beginning,' the King said gravely, `and go on till you come to the end: then stop.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 38 段）

paragraphs.en: These were the verses the White Rabbit read:--
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 39 段）

paragraphs.en: `They told me you had been to her, And mentioned me to him: She gave me a good character, But said I could not swim.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 40 段）

paragraphs.en: He sent them word I had not gone (We know it to be true): If she should push the matter on, What would become of you?
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 41 段）

paragraphs.en: I gave her one, they gave him two, You gave us three or more; They all returned from him to you, Though they were mine before.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 42 段）

paragraphs.en: If I or she should chance to be Involved in this affair, He trusts to you to set them free, Exactly as we were.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 43 段）

paragraphs.en: My notion was that you had been (Before she had this fit) An obstacle that came between Him, and ourselves, and it.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 44 段）

paragraphs.en: Don't let him know she liked them best, For this must ever be A secret, kept from all the rest, Between yourself and me.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 45 段）

paragraphs.en: `That's the most important piece of evidence we've heard yet,' said the King, rubbing his hands; `so now let the jury--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 46 段）

paragraphs.en: `If any one of them can explain it,' said Alice, (she had grown so large in the last few minutes that she wasn't a bit afraid of interrupting him,) `I'll give him sixpence. _I_ don't believe there's an atom of meaning in it.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 47 段）

paragraphs.en: The jury all wrote down on their slates, `SHE doesn't believe there's an atom of meaning in it,' but none of them attempted to explain the paper.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 48 段）

paragraphs.en: `If there's no meaning in it,' said the King, `that saves a world of trouble, you know, as we needn't try to find any. And yet I don't know,' he went on, spreading out the verses on his knee, and looking at them with one eye; `I seem to see some meaning in them, after all. "--SAID I COULD NOT SWIM--" you can't swim, can you?' he added, turning to the Knave.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 49 段）

paragraphs.en: The Knave shook his head sadly. `Do I look like it?' he said. (Which he certainly did NOT, being made entirely of cardboard.)
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 50 段）

paragraphs.en: `All right, so far,' said the King, and he went on muttering over the verses to himself: `"WE KNOW IT TO BE TRUE--" that's the jury, of course-- "I GAVE HER ONE, THEY GAVE HIM TWO--" why, that must be what he did with the tarts, you know--'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 51 段）

paragraphs.en: `But, it goes on "THEY ALL RETURNED FROM HIM TO YOU,"' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 52 段）

paragraphs.en: `Why, there they are!' said the King triumphantly, pointing to the tarts on the table. `Nothing can be clearer than THAT. Then again--"BEFORE SHE HAD THIS FIT--" you never had fits, my dear, I think?' he said to the Queen.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 53 段）

paragraphs.en: `Never!' said the Queen furiously, throwing an inkstand at the Lizard as she spoke. (The unfortunate little Bill had left off writing on his slate with one finger, as he found it made no mark; but he now hastily began again, using the ink, that was trickling down his face, as long as it lasted.)
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 54 段）

paragraphs.en: `Then the words don't FIT you,' said the King, looking round the court with a smile. There was a dead silence.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 55 段）

paragraphs.en: `It's a pun!' the King added in an offended tone, and everybody laughed, `Let the jury consider their verdict,' the King said, for about the twentieth time that day.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 56 段）

paragraphs.en: `No, no!' said the Queen. `Sentence first--verdict afterwards.'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 57 段）

paragraphs.en: `Stuff and nonsense!' said Alice loudly. `The idea of having the sentence first!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 58 段）

paragraphs.en: `Hold your tongue!' said the Queen, turning purple.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 59 段）

paragraphs.en: `I won't!' said Alice.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 60 段）

paragraphs.en: `Off with her head!' the Queen shouted at the top of her voice. Nobody moved.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 61 段）

paragraphs.en: `Who cares for you?' said Alice, (she had grown to her full size by this time.) `You're nothing but a pack of cards!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 62 段）

paragraphs.en: At this the whole pack rose up into the air, and came flying down upon her: she gave a little scream, half of fright and half of anger, and tried to beat them off, and found herself lying on the bank, with her head in the lap of her sister, who was gently brushing away some dead leaves that had fluttered down from the trees upon her face.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 63 段）

paragraphs.en: `Wake up, Alice dear!' said her sister; `Why, what a long sleep you've had!'
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 64 段）

paragraphs.en: `Oh, I've had such a curious dream!' said Alice, and she told her sister, as well as she could remember them, all these strange Adventures of hers that you have just been reading about; and when she had finished, her sister kissed her, and said, `It WAS a curious dream, dear, certainly: but now run in to your tea; it's getting late.' So Alice got up and ran off, thinking while she ran, as well she might, what a wonderful dream it had been.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 65 段）

paragraphs.en: But her sister sat still just as she left her, leaning her head on her hand, watching the setting sun, and thinking of little Alice and all her wonderful Adventures, till she too began dreaming after a fashion, and this was her dream:--
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 66 段）

paragraphs.en: First, she dreamed of little Alice herself, and once again the tiny hands were clasped upon her knee, and the bright eager eyes were looking up into hers--she could hear the very tones of her voice, and see that queer little toss of her head to keep back the wandering hair that WOULD always get into her eyes--and still as she listened, or seemed to listen, the whole place around her became alive the strange creatures of her little sister's dream.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 67 段）

paragraphs.en: The long grass rustled at her feet as the White Rabbit hurried by--the frightened Mouse splashed his way through the neighbouring pool--she could hear the rattle of the teacups as the March Hare and his friends shared their never-ending meal, and the shrill voice of the Queen ordering off her unfortunate guests to execution--once more the pig-baby was sneezing on the Duchess's knee, while plates and dishes crashed around it--once more the shriek of the Gryphon, the squeaking of the Lizard's slate-pencil, and the choking of the suppressed guinea-pigs, filled the air, mixed up with the distant sobs of the miserable Mock Turtle.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 68 段）

paragraphs.en: So she sat on, with closed eyes, and half believed herself in Wonderland, though she knew she had but to open them again, and all would change to dull reality--the grass would be only rustling in the wind, and the pool rippling to the waving of the reeds--the rattling teacups would change to tinkling sheep- bells, and the Queen's shrill cries to the voice of the shepherd boy--and the sneeze of the baby, the shriek of the Gryphon, and all the other queer noises, would change (she knew) to the confused clamour of the busy farm-yard--while the lowing of the cattle in the distance would take the place of the Mock Turtle's heavy sobs.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 69 段）

paragraphs.en: Lastly, she pictured to herself how this same little sister of hers would, in the after-time, be herself a grown woman; and how she would keep, through all her riper years, the simple and loving heart of her childhood: and how she would gather about her other little children, and make THEIR eyes bright and eager with many a strange tale, perhaps even with the dream of Wonderland of long ago: and how she would feel with all their simple sorrows, and find a pleasure in all their simple joys, remembering her own child-life, and the happy summer days.
paragraphs.zh: （第 12 章 · 爱丽丝的证词 第 70 段）
